headline: Every major is red on the day and green on the month, and the crowd calls it greed
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's cleaner than the daily candles suggest. All seven majors sit above nothing uniformly, actually let's be precise: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB all hold above their 200-day lines, while DOGE and ADA sit below theirs, down -70.8% and -77.1% from their 12-month highs respectively. That's a split market, five names in an intact uptrend structure, two still digging out of a hole. ETH, SOL and BNB also carry golden crosses, the 50-day average above the 200-day, which is the slower-moving confirmation that the medium-term trend has actually turned, not just bounced.

Layer on momentum and you find the day's real tension. Every single asset is down on the day (BTC -2.0%, ETH -2.1%, SOL -2.2%, XRP -3.5%, BNB -0.6%, DOGE -3.7%, ADA -3.5%), yet the week and month tell a different story for most: BTC up 1.5% on the week and 22.5% on the month, ETH up 30.8% on the month, SOL up 34.0%. XRP and DOGE are the exceptions, red on both the day and the week (-2.3% and -1.3%) even as they're still up double digits on the month. RSI readings in the low-to-high 60s (BTC 66.4, BNB 70.3) alongside MACD sitting below signal across the board except BNB is a textbook cooling-off: trend intact, short-term thrust fading. Total market cap is down 4.25% over 24 hours, so today's selling wasn't a one-asset story, it was broad.

Positioning adds detail. BTC funding is slightly negative (-2.2% annualized on OKX), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their bets, a small tilt against the crowd's own greed reading. SOL funding is more negative still (-8.3% annualized) despite a long/short ratio of 1.95, an odd pairing: more accounts positioned long, but shorts getting paid, worth just naming as a divergence rather than a signal. XRP and DOGE sit at the other extreme, funding solidly positive (10.0% and 8.7% annualized) with long/short ratios above 2 and 4, crowded long books that also produced the day's most lopsided liquidations: XRP longs lost $713,450 against just $35,436 in shorts over a 7-hour window, DOGE longs lost $377,360 against $32,774 in shorts. That's leverage getting flushed on the long side precisely where the crowd was most stacked.

Flows are where the disagreement with sentiment gets interesting. BTC spot ETFs took in $730.8M on Sep 3, and the five-session net sits at $610.2M inflow, same direction, so this looks like a real bid rather than a one-day print. ETH ETFs added $141.4M on the day with $291.5M over five sessions, though same_direction_days of just 1 means don't lean too hard on continuity there yet. Whale wallets moved $19.46M net off exchanges in the last 24 hours, and the weekly series shows a clear flip: three straight weeks of money moving onto exchanges (Aug 14 through Aug 28, culminating in $1,015M onto exchanges in the week ending Aug 28) followed by $670M moving off exchanges in the week ending Sep 4. Coins leaving exchanges while price falls on the day is the kind of tension worth sitting with: it doesn't say what happens next, only that today's red candles aren't obviously distribution.

Stablecoin float is up 1.46% over 30 days to $310.3B, dry powder building modestly rather than draining, which cuts against a fear-driven exit. And that's the crux: Fear & Greed reads 74, solidly in Greed territory near the top of its 30-day range of 25 to 74, on a day when every major asset is red and total cap dropped over 4%. The gauge is measuring a feeling that hasn't caught up to the tape, or the tape hasn't caught down to the feeling yet. Worth watching from here: whether the ETF inflow streak extends past its current same_direction_days count, whether the weekly whale flow prints another off-exchange week or reverts to the onto-exchange pattern that dominated most of August, and whether XRP or DOGE funding flips negative now that their long-heavy books just got liquidated.
